citations.quote:
The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
> ([[def-choice-function]]).

Written out: for every set $\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,
there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

An equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if
$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.
Here $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that
$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by
itself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.

Assume the data and hypotheses of
[[def-ito-sde-and-strong-solution]] on $[0,T]$, with $T\ge0$, finite
dimensions $d,m\ge1$, Lipschitz constant $L$, and linear-growth constant
$K$. There is a strong solution $X$ on the given filtered probability space.
It is unique up to indistinguishability among strong solutions with the same
initial value and Brownian driver, and it satisfies
$$E\sup_{0\le t\le T}|X_t|^2\le(1+3E|X_0|^2)e^{C_TT},\qquad C_T:=6K^2T+24mK^2.$$
The bound is independent of any later numerical mesh.

Assume AC. Let $T>0$, let $W$ be a standard $d$-dimensional Brownian
motion on a complete usual filtered probability space, with increments after
$s$ independent of $\mathcal F_s$, and let $\theta$ be predictable with
$A_T:=\int_0^T|\theta_s|^2ds<\infty$ almost surely. Set
$$M_t=\int_0^t\theta_s\cdot dW_s,\qquad A_t=\int_0^t|\theta_s|^2ds,\qquad Z_t=\exp(M_t-A_t/2).$$
If $Z$ is a true martingale on $[0,T]$, then $Q=Z_TP$ is equivalent to $P$,
its restriction to $\mathcal F_0$ equals that of $P$, and
$$B_t=W_t-\int_0^t\theta_sds$$
is standard Brownian motion under $Q$ relative to the same filtration.
If $A_T$ is bounded by a deterministic constant, $Z$ is a true martingale.
If additionally $E_PA_T<\infty$, then
$$D(P\|Q)=\frac12E_PA_T.$$

Here is a sufficient condition that permits unbounded $A_T$. Fix a globally
Lipschitz vector field $b:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R^d$, a finite deterministic
grid $0=t_0<\cdots<t_N=T$, and $\eta(t)=t_k$ for
$t_k\le t<t_{k+1}$. Let each of the two path drifts $a,c$ be one of
$0$, $b(X_t)$, or $b(X_{\eta(t)})$. Suppose
$$X_t=X_0+\int_0^ta_s(X)ds+\sqrt2W_t,\qquad E|X_0|^2<\infty,$$
where $X_0$ is $\mathcal F_0$-measurable. For
$\theta_t=(c_t(X)-a_t(X))/\sqrt2$, the exponential $Z$ above is a true
martingale, and under $Q$ the process $X$ has the unique path law with
initial law $\mathcal L_P(X_0)$ and drift $c$ and dispersion $\sqrt2I_d$.
Moreover $E_PA_T<\infty$, so the entropy identity applies. Values of the
piecewise coefficients at grid points do not affect any integral.

Finally, for any probability measures $R\ll S$ and measurable statistic
$F$, relative entropy decreases under pushforward:
$$D(F_\#R\|F_\#S)\le D(R\|S).$$
All equivalence and entropy assertions concern this finite horizon.

Assume the Axiom of Choice and the standing hypothesis (H) of
[[def-elementary-predictable-brownian-integrand]]. Let $m,d\ge1$ be finite
integers, let $B=(B^1,\dots,B^m)$ be a standard $m$-dimensional Brownian motion,
and let $X$ be an $\mathbb R^d$-valued continuous Brownian Ito process
$$X^i_t=X^i_0+\int_0^tb^i_s\,ds+\sum_{k=1}^m\int_0^t\sigma^{ik}_s\,dB^k_s, \qquad i=1,\dots,d,$$
in the sense of [[def-continuous-brownian-ito-process]], including its usual-filtration and almost-sure coefficient-integrability conventions. Let
$f\in C^{1,2}([0,\infty)\times\mathbb R^d)$, meaning that $f,\partial_tf$,
$\partial_if$ and $\partial_i\partial_jf$ ($1\le i,j\le d$) exist and are
continuous. Then, up to indistinguishability, for every $t\ge0$
$$f(t,X_t)=f(0,X_0)+\int_0^t\Bigl(\partial_tf+\sum_ib^i\partial_if+\tfrac12\sum_{i,j}(\sigma\sigma^{\mathsf T})^{ij}\partial_i\partial_jf\Bigr)(s,X_s)\,ds+\sum_{i,k}\int_0^t\partial_if(s,X_s)\sigma^{ik}_s\,dB^k_s,$$
For the displayed integrands, intersect the measurable full events of continuity and the decomposition of $X$, and of coefficient integrability at all integer horizons. Its null complement belongs to $\mathcal F_0$ under the usual conditions. Set $X,X_0,b,\sigma$ to zero there. These representatives preserve all coefficient classes and the decomposition up to indistinguishability, with everywhere continuous $X$ and everywhere locally finite coefficient path integrals. All displayed integrands use these representatives.

The stochastic integrals are localized Ito integrals of the predictable
locally square-integrable integrands $\partial_if(\cdot,X)\sigma^{ik}$, and
$(\sigma\sigma^{\mathsf T})^{ij}_s=\sum_k\sigma^{ik}_s\sigma^{jk}_s$. In
differential form,
$df(t,X_t)=\bigl(\partial_tf+\sum_ib^i\partial_if+\tfrac12\sum_{i,j}(\sigma\sigma^{\mathsf T})^{ij}\partial_i\partial_jf\bigr)(t,X_t)\,dt+\sum_{i,k}\partial_if(t,X_t)\sigma^{ik}_t\,dB^k_t$.

Assume the Axiom of Choice and let $d\ge1$ be a finite integer. An
$\mathbb R^d$-valued process $B=(B_t)_{t\ge0}$ is a **standard
$d$-dimensional Brownian motion** if:

1. $B_0=0$ almost surely;
2. for every finite list $0=t_0<t_1<\cdots<t_n$, the vector increments
   $$B_{t_j}-B_{t_{j-1}},\qquad 1\le j\le n,$$
   are mutually independent and have laws
   $N_d(0,(t_j-t_{j-1})I_d)$; and
3. there is one measurable event $A$ with $P(A)=1$ such that
   $t\mapsto B_t(\omega)$ is continuous from $[0,\infty)$ to
   $\mathbb R^d$ for every $\omega\in A$.

Equivalently, its $d$ coordinate processes $B^\alpha=(B_t^\alpha)_{t\ge0}$
are independent standard one-dimensional Brownian motions. Here independence
of the processes means the following precise assertion. Put
$I=[0,\infty)$ and equip $\mathbb R^I$ with its cylinder sigma-algebra. The
maps
$$ \Phi_\alpha:\Omega\longrightarrow\mathbb R^I, \qquad \Phi_\alpha(\omega)(t)=B_t^\alpha(\omega), \qquad 1\le\alpha\le d, $$
are independent random elements.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $(U,V)$ be a jointly multivariate-normal real
vector with finite-dimensional blocks $U\in\mathbb R^p$ and
$V\in\mathbb R^q$, where $p,q\ge1$. If $\operatorname{Cov}(U_i,V_j)=0$ for every
$1\le i\le p$ and $1\le j\le q$, then $U$ and $V$ are independent. The
covariance matrix may be singular.

Put $C=C([0,\infty),\mathbb R)$, give $C$ the uniform-on-compacts topology,
and write $\pi_t(f)=f(t)$. Then
$$\mathcal B(C)=\sigma(\pi_t:t\ge0)=\sigma(\pi_q:q\in\mathbb Q\cap[0,\infty)).$$
Here each expression on the right denotes the smallest sigma-algebra on $C$
making every displayed coordinate map measurable. No choice principle is used.

Let $\mathcal P$ be a pi-system on $X$. Then
$\lambda_X(\mathcal P)=\sigma_X(\mathcal P)$. Consequently, if $\mathcal D$ is
any lambda-system on $X$ with $\mathcal P\subseteq\mathcal D$, then
$\sigma_X(\mathcal P)\subseteq\mathcal D$.

Assume AC. Let $d\ge1$, $m\in\mathbb R^d$, and let $\Sigma$ be a real symmetric positive-definite $d\times d$ matrix. If $X\sim N_d(m,\Sigma)$, then its law has Lebesgue density
$$f_{m,\Sigma}(x)=(2\pi)^{-d/2}\det(\Sigma)^{-1/2} \exp\!\left(-\tfrac12(x-m)^T\Sigma^{-1}(x-m)\right), \qquad x\in\mathbb R^d.$$

Assume the Axiom of Choice and the standing hypothesis (H) of
[[def-elementary-predictable-brownian-integrand]]. Let $H$ be a predictable
process on $[0,T]$, where $T\ge0$, with $E\int_0^TH_s^2ds<\infty$. Extend $H$ by zero after $T$ when applying the global continuous-version theorem, and let
$M_t=\int_0^tH_s\,dB_s$ be the continuous version of
[[thm-ito-integral-process-has-a-continuous-martingale-version]]. Then
$$E\sup_{0\le t\le T}|M_t|^2\le4\,E\int_0^TH_s^2\,ds .$$
The left-hand side is finite and does not depend on the chosen version, since
any two continuous versions are indistinguishable. Every continuous version of
the integral process satisfies the same bound. The path supremum in this
expectation means its measurable version $S_D=\sup_{q\in D}|M_q|$ on the
countable scaled dyadic grid $D$ (including both endpoints). Continuity
identifies it with the path supremum on a measurable event of probability one.
Indistinguishability here uses that full-event convention, as in the cited
continuous-version theorem, without assuming completeness of the filtration.

Let $(X,\mathcal A,\mu)$ and $(Y,\mathcal B,\nu)$ be sigma-finite measure
spaces, and let $f : X \times Y \to [0,\infty]$ be product-measurable. Then
$x \mapsto \int_Y f_x\,d\nu$ and $y \mapsto \int_X f^y\,d\mu$ are measurable,
and

$$\int_{X \times Y} f\,d(\mu \times \nu) = \int_X \left(\int_Y f_x\,d\nu\right)d\mu = \int_Y \left(\int_X f^y\,d\mu\right)d\nu.$$

Let $(X,\mathcal A,\mu)$ be an arbitrary measure space. All functions below have domain $X$. Let $f$ and $(f_n)$ be measurable complex-valued functions such that
$f_n\to f$ almost everywhere and $|f_n|\le g$ almost everywhere for a single
nonnegative measurable function $g$ with $\int g\,d\mu<+\infty$. Then
$f\in L^1(\mu)$,
$$\int|f_n-f|\,d\mu\longrightarrow0,$$
and hence
$$\int f_n\,d\mu\longrightarrow\int f\,d\mu.$$
If $f:U\subseteq\mathbb R^m\to\mathbb R$ is differentiable at an interior local maximum or minimum $a$, then $\nabla f(a)=0$.

derivations.claim: Put $g=\nabla U$. By [F8], $g(x_\star)=0$, so $\|g(x)\|\le L\|x-x_\star\|$; the equation meets [F1]. Its additive-noise integral equation is $X_s=x-\int_0^s g(X_u)du+\sqrt2 B_s$. For each continuous input path the deterministic Picard iteration converges uniformly on finite intervals: successive differences are bounded by a fixed finite constant times $L^ns^n/n!$, by repeated integration. The limit is the unique solution; subtraction and the same iterative integral bound give $\sup_{s\le t}\|X_s^{x,w}-X_s^{z,v}\|\le e^{Lt}(\|x-z\|+\sqrt2\sup_{s\le t}\|w_s-v_s\|)$. Thus the solution is a continuous function of its initial point and driving path. Its flow composition identity follows from uniqueness of the integral equation. Independent Brownian future increments [F4] now give the Markov and semigroup identities; integration of its Borel solution map against the Brownian law gives a Borel transition kernel. Solutions on integer horizons agree by uniqueness and hence define all $t\ge0$.

Define $\beta_s=\sqrt2(B_s-sB_t/t)$ for $0\le s\le t$. For any finite list of times its coordinates together with $B_t$ are jointly Gaussian and $\operatorname{Cov}(B_s-sB_t/t,B_t)=0$. By [F4] that finite bridge block is independent of $B_t$. Apply [F5] to rational-time cylinders to obtain independence of the entire bridge path and $B_t$. Thus Brownian paths disintegrate explicitly as $$Y_s=x+(s/t)(y-x)+\beta_s$$ when their endpoint has value $y$, with endpoint density $h_t(y-x)$ and bridge law independent of $y$. This identity holds first for cylinder functions by independence and the Gaussian endpoint density, then for all bounded Borel path functions by [F5], and for nonnegative ones by monotone approximation. The bridge has covariance $2(\min(s,u)-su/t)I_d$, which is unchanged when $(s,u)$ is replaced by $(t-s,t-u)$; its mean is zero. Gaussian finite-dimensional laws and [F5] therefore also give equality in law of $\beta_s$ and $\beta_{t-s}$.

Under Brownian law put $Y_s=x+\sqrt2 B_s$. The stochastic exponential with integrand $-g(Y_s)/\sqrt2$ is, by [F3], $$Z_s=\exp\!\left(\frac{U(x)-U(Y_s)}2+\int_0^s\left\{\frac{\Delta U(Y_u)}2-\frac{\|g(Y_u)\|^2}4\right\}du\right).$$ Lipschitz continuity gives $|\partial_{ii}U|\le L$ by taking coordinate difference quotients. Since $U\ge0$, for $s\le t$ this positive local martingale is bounded above by $e^{U(x)/2+tdL/2}$. Stop at increasing energy/local-martingale levels. Dominated convergence [F7] in the stopped martingale identities makes $Z$ a true martingale of mean one. By [F2], under $Z_t$ times Brownian law the process $B_s+\int_0^s g(Y_u)/\sqrt2\,du$ is Brownian, so $Y$ solves the Langevin equation. The explicit unique solution map of step 1.1 identifies its law with $P_t(x,\cdot)$.

Put $H(z)=\Delta U(z)/2-\|g(z)\|^2/4$ and $b_s^{x,y}=x+(s/t)(y-x)+\beta_s$. Combining steps 2.1 and 1.2 gives the density $$p_t(x,y)=h_t(y-x)e^{(U(x)-U(y))/2}\,\mathbb E\exp\!\left(\int_0^t H(b_s^{x,y})ds\right).$$ The integral is a continuous function of $(x,y,\beta)$ in the uniform path topology, since $H$ is continuous and uniformly continuous on each compact set containing the convergent paths. Its exponential is strictly positive and bounded above by $e^{tdL/2}$. Consequently its expectation is positive, finite, and continuous in $(x,y)$ by dominated convergence; the density is jointly Borel. Its integral in $y$ is one by step 2.1. Bridge reversal from step 1.2 interchanges $x,y$ without changing the integral of $H$, and $h_t(y-x)=h_t(x-y)$. Multiplication by $e^{-U(x)}$ proves the asserted symmetry. If $Z<\infty$, Tonelli and the mass-one identity give $$\int Z^{-1}e^{-U(x)}p_t(x,y)dx=Z^{-1}e^{-U(y)}\int p_t(y,x)dx=Z^{-1}e^{-U(y)},$$ proving invariance.

By [F6], $\mathbb E\sup_{s\le t}\|B_s\|^2\le4dt$, and $\sup\|\beta_s\|^2\le8\sup\|B_s\|^2$. With $a_0=\sqrt{64dt}$, Markov's inequality (integrate $1_{\{Y>a_0^2\}}\le Y/a_0^2$ for $Y=\sup\|\beta\|^2$) gives $\Pr(\sup\|\beta\|\le a_0)\ge1/2$. If both endpoints lie in the ball $D=\{\|z-x_\star\|\le R\}$, on this event the bridge lies in the radius $R+a_0$ ball. Therefore $H(b_s^{x,y})\ge-dL/2-L^2(R+a_0)^2/4$ and the bridge expectation in step 3.1 is at least one half times the exponential of $-t[dL/2+L^2(R+a_0)^2/4]$. The heat factor is at least $(4\pi t)^{-d/2}e^{-R^2/t}$ on $D^2$, and $e^{(U(x)-U(y))/2}\ge e^{-\sup_D U/2}>0$. Thus a constant $c>0$ bounds $p_t$ below on $D^2$. Let $\nu$ be normalized Lebesgue measure on $D$ and $\epsilon=\min\{c\operatorname{Leb}(D),1/2\}>0$. Integrating the density over $A\cap D$ proves the stated minorization. The radius is positive, so the normalizing volume is finite and nonzero.

boundaries.reason: The positive dimension and the nonempty Euclidean state space in the Statement exclude an empty-state case.
No zero parameter outside the explicitly stated range is asserted; finite moments and zero signed differences obey the displayed inequalities directly.
The positive integer dimension includes one; no cardinality-one hypothesis or separate combinatorial construction is used.
The Statement has nondegenerate Brownian or Gaussian noise and positive drift parameters; no singular-noise conclusion is asserted.

boundaries.evidence: The Statement requires t>0 and R>0; steps 1.2 and 4.1 include both path endpoints and positive finite minorization volume.
The Statement explicitly assumes AC; step 1.1 carries the exact inherited stochastic or Hahn/Jordan assumption. No unproved measurable selection is used.

boundaries.reason: This is a one-direction implication, with no equivalence assertion.
No converse is asserted.

axioms.reason: AC is inherited through the Brownian, Ito, Gaussian and change-of-measure interfaces. Initial-state solution maps, bridge formulas and compact minorization constants are constructed explicitly.

citations.quote:
The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
> ([[def-choice-function]]).

Written out: for every set $\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,
there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

An equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if
$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.
Here $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that
$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by
itself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.

Assume AC. Let $d\ge1$, $U\in C^2(\mathbb R^d)$, $\nabla U$ be $L$-Lipschitz,
and let $x_\star$ be a global minimizer with $U(x_\star)=0$.
The solutions of
$$dX_t=-\nabla U(X_t)\,dt+\sqrt2\,dB_t,\qquad X_0=x,$$
define a Borel Markov semigroup $P_t$. For every $t>0$ it has a positive
jointly Borel density $p_t(x,y)$ relative to Lebesgue measure, and
$$e^{-U(x)}p_t(x,y)=e^{-U(y)}p_t(y,x).$$
If $Z=\int e^{-U}\,dx\in(0,\infty)$, then $Z^{-1}e^{-U(x)}dx$ is invariant.
For every $R>0$ and $t>0$, there are $\epsilon>0$ and a probability $\nu$ such
that $P_t(x,A)\ge\epsilon\nu(A)$ for every Borel $A$ and
$\|x-x_\star\|\le R$.

Let $d\ge1$, $U\in C^2(\mathbb R^d)$, and suppose $\nabla U$ is $L$-Lipschitz
with $L>0$. Let $x_\star$ be a global minimizer with $U(x_\star)=0$, and
assume the radial condition of
[[lem-ula-potential-coercivity-from-radial-drift]] with parameters
$\rho>0$, $\alpha\in(1,2]$, and $M_\rho\ge0$. For $0<s<1$, set
$$W_s(x)=e^{sU(x)},\qquad \mathscr L_U f(x):=\sum_{i=1}^d\partial_{ii}f(x)-\langle\nabla U(x),\nabla f(x)\rangle,$$
where $\mathscr L_U$ is only the displayed formal differential operator
here. Define
$$K_s:=\max\left\{M_\rho,\left(\frac{2dL}{(1-s)\rho^2}\right)^{1/(2(\alpha-1))}\right\},\qquad \beta_s:=2sdL\exp(sLK_s^2/2).$$
Then for every $x\in\mathbb R^d$,
$$\mathscr L_U W_s(x)\le -sdL W_s(x)+\beta_s\mathbf1_{\{\|x-x_\star\|\le K_s\}}.$$

Let $d\ge1$, $U\in C^2(\mathbb R^d)$, and suppose $\nabla U$ is $L$-Lipschitz
for some $L>0$. Let $x_\star$ be a global minimizer, normalize
$U(x_\star)=0$, and assume that for some $\rho>0$, $\alpha\in(1,2]$,
and $M_\rho\ge0$,
$$\langle\nabla U(x),x-x_\star\rangle\ge\rho\|x-x_\star\|^\alpha\quad\text{whenever }\|x-x_\star\|\ge M_\rho.$$
Then every $x\in\mathbb R^d$ satisfies
$$U(x)\ge\frac{\rho}{\alpha+1}\|x-x_\star\|^\alpha-a_\alpha, \qquad a_\alpha:=\frac{\rho M_\rho^\alpha}{\alpha+1}+\frac{L M_\rho^2}{2}.$$

Assume the Axiom of Choice and the standing hypothesis (H) of
[[def-elementary-predictable-brownian-integrand]]. Let $m,d\ge1$ be finite
integers, let $B=(B^1,\dots,B^m)$ be a standard $m$-dimensional Brownian motion,
and let $X$ be an $\mathbb R^d$-valued continuous Brownian Ito process
$$X^i_t=X^i_0+\int_0^tb^i_s\,ds+\sum_{k=1}^m\int_0^t\sigma^{ik}_s\,dB^k_s, \qquad i=1,\dots,d,$$
in the sense of [[def-continuous-brownian-ito-process]], including its usual-filtration and almost-sure coefficient-integrability conventions. Let
$f\in C^{1,2}([0,\infty)\times\mathbb R^d)$, meaning that $f,\partial_tf$,
$\partial_if$ and $\partial_i\partial_jf$ ($1\le i,j\le d$) exist and are
continuous. Then, up to indistinguishability, for every $t\ge0$
$$f(t,X_t)=f(0,X_0)+\int_0^t\Bigl(\partial_tf+\sum_ib^i\partial_if+\tfrac12\sum_{i,j}(\sigma\sigma^{\mathsf T})^{ij}\partial_i\partial_jf\Bigr)(s,X_s)\,ds+\sum_{i,k}\int_0^t\partial_if(s,X_s)\sigma^{ik}_s\,dB^k_s,$$
For the displayed integrands, intersect the measurable full events of continuity and the decomposition of $X$, and of coefficient integrability at all integer horizons. Its null complement belongs to $\mathcal F_0$ under the usual conditions. Set $X,X_0,b,\sigma$ to zero there. These representatives preserve all coefficient classes and the decomposition up to indistinguishability, with everywhere continuous $X$ and everywhere locally finite coefficient path integrals. All displayed integrands use these representatives.

The stochastic integrals are localized Ito integrals of the predictable
locally square-integrable integrands $\partial_if(\cdot,X)\sigma^{ik}$, and
$(\sigma\sigma^{\mathsf T})^{ij}_s=\sum_k\sigma^{ik}_s\sigma^{jk}_s$. In
differential form,
$df(t,X_t)=\bigl(\partial_tf+\sum_ib^i\partial_if+\tfrac12\sum_{i,j}(\sigma\sigma^{\mathsf T})^{ij}\partial_i\partial_jf\bigr)(t,X_t)\,dt+\sum_{i,k}\partial_if(t,X_t)\sigma^{ik}_t\,dB^k_t$.

Assume the Axiom of Choice and the standing hypothesis (H) of
[[def-elementary-predictable-brownian-integrand]]. Let $H$ be a locally
square-integrable predictable process
[[def-locally-square-integrable-predictable-brownian-integrand]] with localized
integral $H\cdot B$ in the progressively measurable version of
[[thm-localized-ito-integral]], with its measurable-full-event convention
for indistinguishability. The filtration satisfies the usual conditions and
local energy is finite almost surely on every finite horizon, as required by
the local-integrability definition. Let $\tau$ be a
stopping time [[def-continuous-time-stopping-time]]. Then the process
$s\mapsto(H\cdot B)_{s\wedge\tau}$ and the localized integral of the process
$1_{[0,\tau]}H$ are indistinguishable:
$$(H\cdot B)_{t\wedge\tau}=\int_0^t1_{[0,\tau]}(s)H_s\,dB_s\qquad\text{for every }t\ge0\text{, up to indistinguishability}.$$
In particular, for $H$ of finite energy this reduces to the stopping identity
of [[thm-localized-ito-integral]], and for $\tau\equiv\infty$ it is the
definition of the localized integral.

Assume the Axiom of Choice and the standing hypothesis (H) of
[[def-elementary-predictable-brownian-integrand]]. Fix $T>0$. For predictable
$H,K$ with finite energy $E\int_0^TH^2ds,E\int_0^TK^2ds<\infty$ the integrals
$\int_0^TH\,dB$ of
[[def-ito-integral-for-square-integrable-predictable-processes]] satisfy
$$\int_0^T(H+K)\,dB=\int_0^TH\,dB+\int_0^TK\,dB,\qquad \int_0^T(aH)\,dB=a\int_0^TH\,dB\quad(a\in\mathbb R),$$
and the identities are equalities of $L^2(P)$-classes (almost sure
equalities). Moreover the map $H\mapsto\int_0^TH\,dB$ is an isometry,
$$E\Bigl(\int_0^TH\,dB\Bigr)^2=E\int_0^TH^2ds=\|H\|^2_{L^2(\mathrm dt\otimes P)},$$
it takes values in the mean-zero subspace of $L^2(P)$, and the bilinear cross
identity
$$E\Bigl[\Bigl(\int_0^TH\,dB\Bigr)\Bigl(\int_0^TK\,dB\Bigr)\Bigr]=E\int_0^TH_sK_s\,ds$$
holds for all such $H,K$. In particular the image of the map is a closed
subspace of $L^2(P)$ isometric to the predictable $L^2$ space of $H$'s, and
$H\mapsto\int_0^TH\,dB$ is injective up to the $(\mathrm dt\otimes P)$-class.

Let $(f_n)$ be nonnegative measurable functions. Then
$$\int \liminf_{n\to\infty}f_n\,d\mu\le\liminf_{n\to\infty}\int f_n\,d\mu.$$

Let $(X,\mathcal A,\mu)$ and $(Y,\mathcal B,\nu)$ be sigma-finite measure
spaces, and let $f : X \times Y \to [0,\infty]$ be product-measurable. Then
$x \mapsto \int_Y f_x\,d\nu$ and $y \mapsto \int_X f^y\,d\mu$ are measurable,
and

$$\int_{X \times Y} f\,d(\mu \times \nu) = \int_X \left(\int_Y f_x\,d\nu\right)d\mu = \int_Y \left(\int_X f^y\,d\mu\right)d\nu.$$

Assume AC. Let $K$ be a Borel probability kernel on $\mathbb R^d$, $d\ge1$, and let $V:\mathbb R^d\to[1,\infty)$ be finite and Borel. Suppose
$$KV\le aV+b,\qquad 0<a<1,\quad 0\le b<\infty.$$
Suppose that for some $R>\max\{2,2b/(1-a)\}$ the set $D=\{V\le R\}$ is nonempty and there are a probability $\nu$ and $\epsilon_0>0$ such that
$$K(x,A)\ge\epsilon_0\nu(A)\qquad(x\in D,\ A\text{ Borel}).$$
Then $K$ has a unique invariant probability $\pi$, uniqueness being among all Borel probabilities, and $\pi V\le b/(1-a)<\infty$. There are $C<\infty$ and $0<r<1$ such that for all finite-$V$-moment probabilities $\mu,\lambda$ and $n\ge0$,
$$\|\mu K^n-\lambda K^n\|_V\le Cr^n\|\mu-\lambda\|_V.$$
In particular,
$$\|K^n(x,\cdot)-\pi\|_V\le Cr^n\bigl(V(x)+\pi V\bigr).$$
The norm is that of [[def-v-weighted-total-variation-distance]]. Explicitly, put
$$\epsilon=\min\{\epsilon_0,1/2\},\quad\beta=\frac{\epsilon}{2(b+1)},\quad a'=a+\frac{2b}{R},\quad C=\frac{1+\beta}{\beta},$$
$$r=\max\left\{\frac{2+\beta a'R}{2+\beta R},\ 1-\frac{2(\epsilon-\beta b)}{2+\beta R}\right\}.$$
The same contraction holds for finite signed $\eta$ with $\eta(\mathbb R^d)=0$ and $\int V\,d|\eta|<\infty$, with $\mu-\lambda$ replaced by $\eta$.

derivations.claim: Fix a deterministic starting point $x$ and horizon $t$. Stop the continuous solution at its first exit $\tau_n$ from the radius-$n$ ball about $x_\star$, taking $n>\|x-x_\star\|$. Apply [F4] to $e^{a_su}H_s(X_u)$ up to $t\wedge\tau_n$. Its drift is at most $b_se^{a_su}$ by [F2]. Its stochastic integrand is bounded on this stopped finite cylinder, so its expectation is zero. Hence $$\mathbb E_x[e^{a_s(t\wedge\tau_n)}H_s(X_{t\wedge\tau_n})]\le H_s(x)+\frac{b_s}{a_s}(e^{a_st}-1).$$ The globally defined continuous paths in [F1] are bounded on $[0,t]$, so $\tau_n>t$ eventually on each such path. Fatou [F5] and division by $e^{a_st}$ give the claimed semigroup moment bound.

In particular $P_1H_s\le aH_s+b$ with $a=e^{-a_s}\in(0,1)$ and $b=(b_s/a_s)(1-e^{-a_s})<\infty$. Any sufficiently large level set $\{H_s\le R\}$ is contained in a ball by [F3], and inherits the common minorization for $P_1$ from [F1]. The weighted drift-minorization result [F6] therefore gives an invariant law $\xi_s$ with finite $H_s$ moment and constants $M_s<\infty$, $r_s\in(0,1)$ such that $$\|\mu P_n-\nu P_n\|_{H_s}\le M_sr_s^n\|\mu-\nu\|_{H_s}\qquad(n\in\mathbb N).$$ Since [F1] already makes $\pi$ invariant and [F6] gives uniqueness among every invariant probability, $\xi_s=\pi$ and $\pi H_s<\infty$.

For $0\le u<1$, step 1.1 gives $P_uH_s\le H_s+b_s/a_s\le(1+b_s/a_s)H_s$, since $H_s\ge1$. For every Borel $f$ with $|f|\le H_s$, therefore $|P_uf|\le(1+b_s/a_s)H_s$. Taking the test-function supremum shows $$\|\mu P_u-\nu P_u\|_{H_s}\le(1+b_s/a_s)\|\mu-\nu\|_{H_s}.$$ All integrals are finite by step 1.1 and [F5]. Write $t=n+u$ with $n=\lfloor t\rfloor$ and apply this estimate after the integer contraction in step 2.1. With $v_s=-\log r_s>0$ and $C_s=M_s(1+b_s/a_s)r_s^{-1}$, the result follows from $r_s^n\le r_s^{-1}e^{-v_st}$. This includes $t=0$ and all stated finite-moment initial laws.

citations.quote:
The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
> ([[def-choice-function]]).

Written out: for every set $\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,
there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

An equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if
$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.
Here $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that
$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by
itself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.

Assume AC ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $d\ge1$, let $U:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R$ be Borel measurable
in the sense of [[def-borel-and-lebesgue-measurable-function-on-rn]] and
continuously differentiable with
$$0<Z_U:=\int_{\mathbb R^d}e^{-U(x)}\,dx<\infty,$$
and define the target probability
$$\pi_U(dx):=Z_U^{-1}e^{-U(x)}\,dx.$$
This is the measure with density $Z_U^{-1}e^{-U}$ relative to Lebesgue measure
([[def-measure-with-density]] and [[def-lebesgue-measure-and-the-lebesgue-sigma-algebra]]);
the probability-measure convention is [[def-probability-measure]], and the
normalizer makes its total mass one.
Given a step size $\gamma>0$, an initial state $X_0\in\mathbb R^d$, and an
IID sequence $Z_1,Z_2,\ldots\sim N_d(0,I_d)$, using the multivariate-normal
law of [[def-multivariate-normal-law]] and standard-normal convention of
[[def-standard-normal-and-normal-laws]], repeat for $k\ge0$:

1. Compute the Euclidean gradient $\nabla U(X_k)$ using the convention of
   [[def-jacobian-matrix-and-gradient]].
2. Take the fixed-step gradient update
   $\widetilde X_{k+1}=X_k-\gamma\nabla U(X_k)$, the fixed-step branch of
   [[alg-gradient-descent]].
3. Set
   $$X_{k+1}=\widetilde X_{k+1}+\sqrt{2\gamma}\,Z_{k+1}.$$

The one-step transition law is
$$Q_\gamma(x,\cdot)=N_d(x-\gamma\nabla U(x),2\gamma I_d).$$
The procedure applies the proposal at every step and has no accept/reject
correction. The probability-kernel and density properties of $Q_\gamma$ are
proved in [[lem-langevin-gaussian-proposal-kernel]].

Assume AC and the hypotheses of [[alg-unadjusted-langevin-algorithm]]. For
$\gamma>0$, its proposal family $Q_\gamma$ is a probability kernel on
$\mathbb R^d$ and has the everywhere positive finite jointly continuous
Lebesgue density
$$q_\gamma(y\mid x)=(4\pi\gamma)^{-d/2}\exp\!\left(-\frac{\|y-x+\gamma\nabla U(x)\|^2}{4\gamma}\right).$$

Assume AC. Let $d\ge1$, $U\in C^2(\mathbb R^d)$, and suppose $\nabla U$ is
$L$-Lipschitz for $L>0$. Let $x_\star$ be a global minimizer with
$U(x_\star)=0$. Suppose that for $\rho>0$, $\alpha\in(1,2]$, and
$M_\rho\ge0$,
$$\langle\nabla U(x),x-x_\star\rangle\ge\rho\|x-x_\star\|^\alpha \quad\text{if }\|x-x_\star\|\ge M_\rho.$$
For $0<\gamma<L^{-1}$, define
$$K_\gamma:=\max\left\{M_\rho, \left(\frac{2d[-\log(1-L\gamma)]/\gamma+4}{\rho^2}\right)^{1/(2(\alpha-1))}\right\}, \qquad V(x):=e^{U(x)/2},$$
and let $P_\gamma$ be the ULA proposal kernel. Then
$$P_\gamma V(x):=\int V(y)P_\gamma(x,dy) \le e^{-\gamma}V(x) +e^{LK_\gamma^2/4}(1-L\gamma)^{-d/2} \mathbf1_{\{\|x-x_\star\|\le K_\gamma\}}.$$

Let $d\ge1$, $U\in C^2(\mathbb R^d)$, and suppose $\nabla U$ is $L$-Lipschitz
for some $L>0$. Let $x_\star$ be a global minimizer, normalize
$U(x_\star)=0$, and assume that for some $\rho>0$, $\alpha\in(1,2]$,
and $M_\rho\ge0$,
$$\langle\nabla U(x),x-x_\star\rangle\ge\rho\|x-x_\star\|^\alpha\quad\text{whenever }\|x-x_\star\|\ge M_\rho.$$
Then every $x\in\mathbb R^d$ satisfies
$$U(x)\ge\frac{\rho}{\alpha+1}\|x-x_\star\|^\alpha-a_\alpha, \qquad a_\alpha:=\frac{\rho M_\rho^\alpha}{\alpha+1}+\frac{L M_\rho^2}{2}.$$

Assume AC. Let $K$ be a Borel probability kernel on $\mathbb R^d$, $d\ge1$, and let $V:\mathbb R^d\to[1,\infty)$ be finite and Borel. Suppose
$$KV\le aV+b,\qquad 0<a<1,\quad 0\le b<\infty.$$
Suppose that for some $R>\max\{2,2b/(1-a)\}$ the set $D=\{V\le R\}$ is nonempty and there are a probability $\nu$ and $\epsilon_0>0$ such that
$$K(x,A)\ge\epsilon_0\nu(A)\qquad(x\in D,\ A\text{ Borel}).$$
Then $K$ has a unique invariant probability $\pi$, uniqueness being among all Borel probabilities, and $\pi V\le b/(1-a)<\infty$. There are $C<\infty$ and $0<r<1$ such that for all finite-$V$-moment probabilities $\mu,\lambda$ and $n\ge0$,
$$\|\mu K^n-\lambda K^n\|_V\le Cr^n\|\mu-\lambda\|_V.$$
In particular,
$$\|K^n(x,\cdot)-\pi\|_V\le Cr^n\bigl(V(x)+\pi V\bigr).$$
The norm is that of [[def-v-weighted-total-variation-distance]]. Explicitly, put
$$\epsilon=\min\{\epsilon_0,1/2\},\quad\beta=\frac{\epsilon}{2(b+1)},\quad a'=a+\frac{2b}{R},\quad C=\frac{1+\beta}{\beta},$$
$$r=\max\left\{\frac{2+\beta a'R}{2+\beta R},\ 1-\frac{2(\epsilon-\beta b)}{2+\beta R}\right\}.$$
The same contraction holds for finite signed $\eta$ with $\eta(\mathbb R^d)=0$ and $\int V\,d|\eta|<\infty$, with $\mu-\lambda$ replaced by $\eta$.

For every $m\in\mathbb N$ and every real $a>0$,
$$\frac{x^m}{\exp(ax)}\longrightarrow0\qquad(x\to+\infty).$$
If $f:U\subseteq\mathbb R^m\to\mathbb R$ is differentiable at an interior local maximum or minimum $a$, then $\nabla f(a)=0$.

Let $f:U\to V\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be totally differentiable at $a\in U$ and let $g:V\to\mathbb R^p$ be totally differentiable at $f(a)$. Then $g\circ f$ is totally differentiable at $a$ and

$$D(g\circ f)(a)=Dg(f(a))\circ Df(a).$$

Let $a<b$. Suppose $G:[a,b]\to\mathbb R$ is continuous on $[a,b]$ and differentiable on $(a,b)$. If $f:[a,b]\to\mathbb R$ is Riemann integrable and

$$f(x)=G'(x)\qquad(a<x<b),$$

then

$$\int_a^b f=G(b)-G(a).$$

No derivative of $G$ at either endpoint is assumed, and the two endpoint values assigned to the integrable extension $f$ do not enter the conclusion.

Let $n \in \mathbb{N}$ and let $x, y \in \mathbb{R}^{n}$, with the Euclidean
inner product and the Euclidean norm as in [[def-euclidean-inner-product]]. Then:

1. **Cauchy-Schwarz.**
   $$\lvert\langle x,y\rangle\rvert \;\le\; \lVert x\rVert_2\,\lVert y\rVert_2 ,$$
   with equality if and only if there is a pair $(\lambda,\mu) \ne (0,0)$ of
   reals with $\lambda x_k = \mu y_k$ for every $k < n$.
2. **$\lVert\cdot\rVert_2$ is a norm on $\mathbb{R}^{n}$**
   ([[def-norm-and-normed-space]]), for **every** $n \in \mathbb{N}$; the metric
   it induces is $d_2$ of [[lem-metrics-on-rn]] whenever $n \ge 1$.
3. **Parallelogram law.**
   $$\lVert x+y\rVert_2^{2} + \lVert x-y\rVert_2^{2} \;=\; 2\lVert x\rVert_2^{2} + 2\lVert y\rVert_2^{2} .$$
4. **Polarisation.**
   $$\langle x,y\rangle \;=\; \tfrac14\Bigl(\lVert x+y\rVert_2^{2} - \lVert x-y\rVert_2^{2}\Bigr),$$
   so the inner product is recovered from the norm it induces.

**Clause 1 is a citation, not a new proof.** The inequality and its equality case
are the published [[thm-cauchy-schwarz-finite]], stated there for two lists of
reals; all that happens below is that it is read in the vector notation of
[[def-euclidean-inner-product]]. Re-proving it here would put two proofs of one
statement in the library.

Assume AC. Let $d\ge1$, $m\in\mathbb R^d$, and let $\Sigma$ be a real symmetric positive-definite $d\times d$ matrix. If $X\sim N_d(m,\Sigma)$, then its law has Lebesgue density
$$f_{m,\Sigma}(x)=(2\pi)^{-d/2}\det(\Sigma)^{-1/2} \exp\!\left(-\tfrac12(x-m)^T\Sigma^{-1}(x-m)\right), \qquad x\in\mathbb R^d.$$
$$\int_{-\infty}^{\infty}e^{-x^2}\,dx=\sqrt\pi.$$

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let
$U,V \subseteq \mathbb R^n$ be open and let $T : U \to V$ be a
$C^1$ diffeomorphism. For every nonnegative Lebesgue measurable
$f : V \to [0,\infty]$,
$$ \int_V f(y)\,d\lambda_n(y) = \int_U f(T(x))\,|\det DT(x)|\,d\lambda_n(x). $$

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let
$m,n \ge 1$. Under the identification
$$\mathbb R^{m+n}=\mathbb R^m \times \mathbb R^n,$$
the product measure $\lambda_m \times \lambda_n$ and the Euclidean Lebesgue
measure $\lambda_{m+n}$ agree on every Borel subset of $\mathbb R^{m+n}$.

Let $(X,\mathcal A,\mu)$ and $(Y,\mathcal B,\nu)$ be sigma-finite measure
spaces, and let $f : X \times Y \to [0,\infty]$ be product-measurable. Then
$x \mapsto \int_Y f_x\,d\nu$ and $y \mapsto \int_X f^y\,d\mu$ are measurable,
and

$$\int_{X \times Y} f\,d(\mu \times \nu) = \int_X \left(\int_Y f_x\,d\nu\right)d\mu = \int_Y \left(\int_X f^y\,d\mu\right)d\nu.$$

derivations.claim: Fix $\gamma$. Dropping the indicator in [F2] gives a global drift $R_\gamma V\le e^{-\gamma}V+b_\gamma$ with finite $b_\gamma$. Each sufficiently large V-sublevel is contained in a compact ball by [F3]. On the product of that starting ball and any fixed positive-radius target ball, the continuous positive density [F1] has a positive minimum: explicitly its Gaussian exponent is bounded because both balls and the continuous gradient are bounded. Restriction to the target ball and normalization of its positive finite volume give a common minorization. These are precisely the drift and minorization hypotheses for the weight V.

By [F6], $g(x_\star)=0$, and therefore Lipschitz continuity gives $\|g(x)\|\le L\|x-x_\star\|$. If $r=\|x-x_\star\|$ is positive and at least the radial radius, Cauchy–Schwarz and the radial hypothesis give $\|g(x)\|r\ge\langle g(x),x-x_\star\rangle\ge\rho r^\alpha$, so $\|g(x)\|\ge\rho r^{\alpha-1}$. For $h=y-x$, integrate the derivative along $x+th$ and subtract $\langle g(x),h\rangle$ to obtain $$U(y)-U(x)-\langle g(x),h\rangle=\int_0^1\langle g(x+th)-g(x),h\rangle dt\le\frac{L}{2}\|h\|^2.$$

Completing the square, [F7] gives for $c<1/2$ and scalar v the identity $$(2\pi)^{-1/2}\int_{\mathbb R}e^{-(1/2-c)z^2+vz}dz=(1-2c)^{-1/2}e^{v^2/(2(1-2c))}.$$ Finite multiplication and Tonelli therefore give $\mathbb E e^{c\|Z\|^2+\langle v,Z\rangle}=(1-2c)^{-d/2}e^{\|v\|^2/(2(1-2c))}$ for $Z\sim N_d(0,I_d)$.
Apply [F4] to the fixed-step kernel and weight V verified in step 1.1. It supplies a unique invariant probability $\pi_\gamma$ with finite V moment.

Put $g=\nabla U(x)$ and $H_s=e^{sU}$ for $0<s<1$ with $2sL\gamma<1$. Apply step 1.2 to $Y=x-\gamma g+\sqrt{2\gamma}Z$, multiply by s, and exponentiate. Step 1.3, with quadratic coefficient $sL\gamma$ and linear coefficient $s\sqrt{2\gamma}(1-L\gamma)g$, gives $$\frac{R_\gamma H_s(x)}{H_s(x)}\le(1-2sL\gamma)^{-d/2}\exp\!\left(-\frac{s\gamma(1-s-L\gamma/2)}{1-2sL\gamma}\|g\|^2\right).$$ The coefficient follows by combining $s\gamma(-1+L\gamma/2)$ with $s^2\gamma(1-L\gamma)^2/(1-2sL\gamma)$ over the common denominator. All Gaussian integrals are finite under $2sL\gamma<1$.

For $s=1/2$, step 2.2 reduces to $$R_\gamma V\le V\exp\!\left(\tfrac d2[-\log(1-L\gamma)]-\tfrac\gamma4\|g\|^2\right).$$ If $\gamma\le\gamma_0$, then $-\log(1-L\gamma)\le2L\gamma$, since $-\log(1-z)=\int_0^z(1-u)^{-1}du\le2z$ for $z\le1/2$. Choose a radius R at least the radial radius and large enough that $\rho^2R^{2(\alpha-1)}/4\ge dL+1$. Outside this ball step 1.2 makes the exponent at most $-\gamma$. Inside it let $M=\sup_{\|x-x_\star\|\le R}V(x)<\infty$. Since $e^{a\gamma}-e^{-\gamma}=\int_{-\gamma}^{a\gamma}e^u du\le(a+1)\gamma e^{a\gamma_0}$ for $a=dL$, the preceding bound gives $$R_\gamma V\le e^{-\gamma}V+b\gamma,\qquad b=M(dL+1)e^{dL\gamma_0},$$ uniformly for small steps. Integrate against the finite-V invariant law from step 2.1 to obtain $\pi_\gamma V\le b\gamma/(1-e^{-\gamma})\le b e^{\gamma_0}$, using $1-e^{-\gamma}=\int_0^\gamma e^{-u}du\ge\gamma e^{-\gamma_0}$. This proves the first uniform bound.

For $s=1/4$ and $0<\gamma<L^{-1}$, the logarithm of the prefactor in step 2.2 is at most $dL\gamma/2$, by the same integral estimate with $z=L\gamma/2<1/2$. Moreover $s(1-s-L\gamma/2)/(1-2sL\gamma)\ge1/16$, because the numerator is at least $1/16$ and the denominator is at most one. Choose R' at least the radial radius such that $\rho^2(R')^{2(\alpha-1)}/16\ge dL/2+1$. Outside this ball $R_\gamma W\le e^{-\gamma}W$; inside use $M'=\sup_{\|x-x_\star\|\le R'}W(x)$ and the exponential-difference estimate from step 3.1 with $a=dL/2$ and upper horizon $L^{-1}$. Thus $$R_\gamma W\le e^{-\gamma}W+b'\gamma,\qquad b'=M'(dL/2+1)e^{d/2},$$ for the whole step range. Since $W\le V$, its invariant moment is finite by step 2.1. Integrating and using $1-e^{-\gamma}\ge\gamma e^{-1/L}$ gives $\pi_\gamma W\le b'e^{1/L}$, uniformly for every allowed step.

Put $r=\|x-x_\star\|$. For $r\ge1$, [F3] gives $V(x)\ge e^{-C/2}e^{cr^\alpha/2}\ge e^{-C/2}e^{cr/2}$ because $\alpha>1$. By [F5], $r^2/e^{cr/2}$ is bounded on $[1,\infty)$; on $[0,1]$ use $r^2\le1\le V$. Thus $r^2\le A V$ for some finite A. The Lipschitz bound in step 1.2 gives $\|\nabla U(x)\|^2\le L^2r^2$. Taking $M_g=(1+L^2)A$, $M_V=be^{\gamma_0}$ and $M_W=b'e^{1/L}$ proves all asserted estimates. All constants depend only on the fixed potential and its displayed parameters.

citations.quote:
The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
> ([[def-choice-function]]).

Written out: for every set $\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,
there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

An equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if
$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.
Here $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that
$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by
itself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.

Assume AC ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $d\ge1$, let $U:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R$ be Borel measurable
in the sense of [[def-borel-and-lebesgue-measurable-function-on-rn]] and
continuously differentiable with
$$0<Z_U:=\int_{\mathbb R^d}e^{-U(x)}\,dx<\infty,$$
and define the target probability
$$\pi_U(dx):=Z_U^{-1}e^{-U(x)}\,dx.$$
This is the measure with density $Z_U^{-1}e^{-U}$ relative to Lebesgue measure
([[def-measure-with-density]] and [[def-lebesgue-measure-and-the-lebesgue-sigma-algebra]]);
the probability-measure convention is [[def-probability-measure]], and the
normalizer makes its total mass one.
Given a step size $\gamma>0$, an initial state $X_0\in\mathbb R^d$, and an
IID sequence $Z_1,Z_2,\ldots\sim N_d(0,I_d)$, using the multivariate-normal
law of [[def-multivariate-normal-law]] and standard-normal convention of
[[def-standard-normal-and-normal-laws]], repeat for $k\ge0$:

1. Compute the Euclidean gradient $\nabla U(X_k)$ using the convention of
   [[def-jacobian-matrix-and-gradient]].
2. Take the fixed-step gradient update
   $\widetilde X_{k+1}=X_k-\gamma\nabla U(X_k)$, the fixed-step branch of
   [[alg-gradient-descent]].
3. Set
   $$X_{k+1}=\widetilde X_{k+1}+\sqrt{2\gamma}\,Z_{k+1}.$$

The one-step transition law is
$$Q_\gamma(x,\cdot)=N_d(x-\gamma\nabla U(x),2\gamma I_d).$$
The procedure applies the proposal at every step and has no accept/reject
correction. The probability-kernel and density properties of $Q_\gamma$ are
proved in [[lem-langevin-gaussian-proposal-kernel]].

Assume AC and the hypotheses of
[[lem-ula-fixed-step-gaussian-kernel-exponential-drift]]. Let $R_\gamma$ be
the ULA kernel, $V=e^{U/2}$, $W=e^{U/4}$, and $\gamma_0=(2L)^{-1}$.
For every $0<\gamma<L^{-1}$ there is a unique invariant probability
$\pi_\gamma$, and $\pi_\gamma V<\infty$.
There are finite constants $M_V,M_W,M_g$, independent of $\gamma$, such that
$$\sup_{0<\gamma\le\gamma_0}\pi_\gamma V\le M_V,\qquad \sup_{0<\gamma<L^{-1}}\pi_\gamma W\le M_W,\qquad \|\nabla U(x)\|^2+\|x-x_\star\|^2\le M_gV(x).$$

Assume AC and the smoothness, minimizer, normalization and radial hypotheses of
[[lem-langevin-potential-exponential-generator-drift]]. Suppose
$Z=\int e^{-U(x)}dx\in(0,\infty)$ and put $\pi(dx)=Z^{-1}e^{-U(x)}dx$.
For $0<s<1$, write $H_s=e^{sU}$ and let $a_s=sdL$ and $b_s=\beta_s$ be the
constants in that lemma. The Langevin semigroup of
[[lem-langevin-diffusion-density-reversibility-and-compact-minorization]] satisfies
$$P_tH_s(x)\le e^{-a_st}H_s(x)+\frac{b_s}{a_s}(1-e^{-a_st}),\qquad \pi H_s<\infty.$$
There are $C_s<\infty$ and $v_s>0$, depending on the potential and $s$, such that
for any probability measures $\mu,\nu$ with finite $H_s$ moments and any $t\ge0$,
$$\|\mu P_t-\nu P_t\|_{H_s}\le C_se^{-v_st}\|\mu-\nu\|_{H_s}.$$
The norm is [[def-v-weighted-total-variation-distance]].

Assume AC. Let $d\ge1$, let $U\in C^1(\mathbb R^d)$ have globally
$L$-Lipschitz gradient $g=\nabla U$, and let
$0=t_0<\cdots<t_N=T$, $\gamma_{k+1}=t_{k+1}-t_k$,
$\eta(t)=t_k$ on $[t_k,t_{k+1})$. On a complete usual filtered Brownian
space, start with an $\mathcal F_0$-measurable $X_0$ satisfying
$E|X_0|^2<\infty$ and interpolate the Euler recursion by
$$X_t=X_{t_k}-(t-t_k)g(X_{t_k})+\sqrt2(W_t-W_{t_k}),\qquad t_k\le t\le t_{k+1}.$$
Let $\mathsf E$ be its law on $C([0,T],\mathbb R^d)$ and let $\mathsf D$
be the path law of $dY_t=-g(Y_t)dt+\sqrt2dB_t$ with the same initial law.
Then $\mathsf E$ and $\mathsf D$ are equivalent and
$$D(\mathsf E\|\mathsf D)=\frac14E\int_0^T|g(X_t)-g(X_{\eta(t)})|^2dt\le\frac{L^2}{4}\sum_{k=0}^{N-1}\left\{\frac{\gamma_{k+1}^3}{3}E|g(X_{t_k})|^2+d\gamma_{k+1}^2\right\}.$$
In particular the same upper bound holds for
$D(\mathcal L(X_T)\|\mathcal L(Y_T))$.
The expectations in the bound are under the Euler law; its gradient moments
are finite under the stated hypotheses. No convexity or stationarity is
required, and the direction of the relative entropy is Euler relative to
diffusion.

Assume AC. Let $\mu,\nu$ be Borel probability measures on $\mathbb R^d$,
and let $W:\mathbb R^d\to[1,\infty)$ be Borel measurable with
$\int W^2\,d\mu+\int W^2\,d\nu<\infty$. Then
$$\|\mu-\nu\|_W\le\sqrt{2\left(\int W^2\,d\mu+\int W^2\,d\nu\right)D(\mu\|\nu)},$$
where $\mu,\nu$ are probability measures in the sense of [[def-probability-measure]],
$\|\cdot\|_W$ is defined in
[[def-v-weighted-total-variation-distance]] and $D(\mu\|\nu)$ is the
directional relative entropy of [[def-kullback-leibler-divergence]]. If
$D(\mu\|\nu)=+\infty$, the inequality is understood in the extended-real
sense and is immediate.

Let $d\ge1$, let $W:\mathbb R^d\to[1,\infty)$ be Borel measurable, and let
$\mu,\nu$ be Borel probability measures on $\mathbb R^d$ with
$\int W\,d\mu<\infty$ and $\int W\,d\nu<\infty$. Define their
**$W$-weighted total-variation distance** by
$$\|\mu-\nu\|_W:=\sup_{f\,\mathrm{Borel},\ |f|\le W}\left|\int f\,d\mu-\int f\,d\nu\right|.$$
The moment hypotheses make every integral in the supremum finite. This is the
signed-measure test-function norm used in weighted-variation bounds. For
$W\equiv1$ it has the usual factor of two relative to the event-supremum
probability distance in [[def-total-variation-distance-for-probability-laws]].
Here a Borel probability measure is in the sense of [[def-probability-measure]],
on the Borel sigma-algebra of [[def-borel-sigma-algebra]].

derivations.claim: By [F1], for each allowed step the unique invariant probability $\pi_\gamma$ exists and has finite V moment, hence finite W moment since $1\le W\le V$. By [F2], $\pi_U V<\infty$, so its W moment is finite too. Choose a fixed $T_0>0$ so that $C_We^{-v_WT_0}\le1/2$, possible because $v_W>0$. All these constants depend only on the potential and its hypotheses.

First suppose $0<\gamma\le\gamma_0$. Put $m=\lceil T_0/\gamma\rceil$ and $T=m\gamma$, so $T_0\le T<T_0+\gamma\le T_0+\gamma_0$. Start Euler with law $\mu=\pi_\gamma$, independently of its Brownian increments; every grid-time law is $\mu$ by invariance. Its second moment is finite by [F1], since $\|x\|^2\le2\|x-x_\star\|^2+2\|x_\star\|^2$. Moreover $\mathbb E\|\nabla U(X_k)\|^2\le M_gM_V$ at every grid time. Apply [F3] to the diffusion with the same initial law. Euler's endpoint law is $\mu$ and diffusion's is $\mu P_T$, giving $$D(\mu\|\mu P_T)\le\frac{L^2}{4}m\left(\frac{\gamma^3}{3}M_gM_V+d\gamma^2\right)\le K_D\gamma,\qquad K_D=\frac{L^2}{4}(T_0+\gamma_0)\left(d+\frac{\gamma_0}{3}M_gM_V\right).$$ The initial Brownian/Gaussian construction uses only the inherited AC assumption.

By [F1], $\mu V\le M_V$; by [F2], $(\mu P_T)V\le M_V+B_V$. Weighted Pinsker [F4] and step 2.1 therefore imply $$\|\mu-\mu P_T\|_W\le K_E\sqrt\gamma,\qquad K_E=\sqrt{2(2M_V+B_V)K_D}.$$ Since $\pi_U P_T=\pi_U$, the contraction [F2], the choice of $T_0$, and $T\ge T_0$ give $$\|\mu-\pi_U\|_W\le K_E\sqrt\gamma+\|\mu P_T-\pi_U P_T\|_W\le K_E\sqrt\gamma+\tfrac12\|\mu-\pi_U\|_W.$$ The last norm is finite by step 1.1, so subtraction yields $\|\pi_\gamma-\pi_U\|_W\le2K_E\sqrt\gamma$ throughout the small-step range.

If $\gamma_0<\gamma<L^{-1}$, [F1] and [F5] give $\|\pi_\gamma-\pi_U\|_W\le M_W+\pi_U W\le (M_W+\pi_U W)\gamma_0^{-1/2}\sqrt\gamma$. Together with step 3.1, this proves the stated bound with $$C=\max\{2K_E,(M_W+\pi_U W)\gamma_0^{-1/2}\}<\infty,$$ independent of $\gamma$ over the entire specified open interval. Step 1.1 supplies both finite weight moments and uniqueness/existence for every such step.
